sections.h2: Which offices touch an Alachua County tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices split the work: the Property Appraiser values the property and decides exemptions, the Tax Collector bills and collects, and the Clerk records deeds and collects documentary stamp tax at recording.

The Alachua County Tax Collector's site explains that the Property Appraiser prepares the real estate and tangible personal property rolls, which fix ownership, mailing address, legal description and value. Taxes equal taxable value, after exemptions, times the millage rate set by each taxing authority. If no bill arrives in November, the Tax Collector's page gives (352) 374-5236 as the number to call.

  • Value, ownership and exemptions: Alachua County Property Appraiser (acpafl.org), which also offers a free Title Alert for ownership changes.
  • Bills, payment plans and deferral: Alachua County Tax Collector.
  • Recorded deeds and doc stamps: Clerk of the Circuit Court, which also runs foreclosure and tax deed sales.

sections.h2: When are Alachua County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are normally mailed by November 1, the full amount is due March 31, and unpaid real estate tax turns delinquent April 1.

Discounts follow the postmark. Once a bill is delinquent, the office says a 3 percent minimum charge is added on April 1 and an advertising charge in May, and the date the payment is received controls the amount.

sections.h2: What are the Alachua County millage rates?
sections.html:
Alachua County's own 2026 TRIM explainer lists a 2025 countywide millage of 7.6000 mills and a proposed 2026 rollback rate of 7.2107 mills, which it describes as the tenth straight year of a lower countywide rate.

Treat the 2026 figure as proposed until the final adopted rate appears on your bill or the Tax Collector's site. The same article notes that a TRIM notice carries several taxing authorities, so the county is only one line on it. Homes inside a city add that city's levy, and the explainer says that for Gainesville certain charges once on monthly utility bills now appear on the notice.

Some owners in unincorporated areas also see a Law Enforcement Municipal Services Taxing Unit line, which the county lists at a proposed 3.5678 mills. Non-ad valorem items such as county fire, solid waste and stormwater are charged by assessment, not millage.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and deadlines should an Alachua County owner know?
sections.html:
Homestead and other exemption applications are due to the county property appraiser by March 1, and you must have made the home your permanent residence by January 1 (Florida Department of Revenue).

  • The homestead exemption is up to $50,000: the first $25,000 applies to all levies including school, and the second $25,000 applies to assessed value above $50,000 for non-school levies.
  • Save Our Homes caps yearly growth in assessed value at the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The DOR chart lists a 2.7 percent cap for 2026.
  • A sale, foreclosure or other change of ownership resets the property to just value the next January 1, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses.
  • Portability lets an owner carry the Save Our Homes benefit to a new homestead established within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was given up.
  • Disabled veterans, deployed servicemembers and seniors can qualify for added relief. A city or county ordinance sets the senior exemption.

Renting out a homestead ends the exemption, so a seller who moved out should ask the Property Appraiser how the status stands.

sections.h2: Can Alachua County owners pay in installments or defer tax?
sections.html:
Yes. The Tax Collector offers a quarterly installment plan and a homestead tax deferral, each with its own rules.

For installments, prior year taxes must exceed $100 and applications are due by April 30 of the tax year. Discounts printed on the page are 6 percent on the June 30 payment, 4.5 percent on the September 30 payment, 3 percent on the December 31 payment and none on the March 31 payment.

For deferral, the property must qualify for homestead, the primary mortgage cannot exceed 70 percent of assessed value, and the application is due by March 31. Interest accrues on deferred tax, capped at 7 percent a year, and the page says everything deferred comes due with any change in homestead eligibility, use or ownership. That means a sale triggers payoff at closing.

sections.h2: What should landlords in Alachua County know about tax on rentals?
sections.html:
Rental houses carry two exposures: the real estate bill and tangible personal property tax on furniture, fixtures and equipment inside a rental.

The Tax Collector explains that the Property Appraiser values tangible property each January 1 and that a return filed between January 1 and April 1 earns an exemption of up to $25,000. Late or missing returns bring penalties and loss of that exemption. Unpaid tangible tax turns delinquent April 1 with a $10 fee and 1.5 percent monthly interest, and a 20 percent collection fee is added May 1.

Landlords selling a rental should note that, per the same page, the tangible tax lien follows the property and survives a sale, and any proration between buyer and seller is handled at closing. Owners with rentals can also ask the county's waste collection office (352-338-3233) about assessment discounts for a vacant residential rental.

sections.h2: What happens when Alachua County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector advertises delinquent parcels and, on or before June 1, holds an online tax certificate sale on lienhub.com, with bidding starting at 18 percent and going down.

The winning bidder pays the tax and earns interest, and the certificate becomes a first lien on the property. The page says the holder may apply for a tax deed once two or more years have passed since delinquency, and an unredeemed property is sold at public auction. To clear a certificate, the owner pays the Tax Collector the tax, interest, costs and charges.

Under Florida law a certificate holder may not demand payment from the owner until two years after April 1 of the issue year. A seller with a certificate on the house can usually clear it from sale proceeds, and the payoff figure comes from the Tax Collector's office.

sections.h2: How is tax handled when an Alachua County house sells?
sections.html:
The bill goes to whoever is on the roll, and the two sides settle the split at the closing table.

Florida sets a deed documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county except Miami-Dade, paid to the clerk at recording, and all parties to the deed are liable regardless of who agrees to pay. A buyer whose mortgage pays taxes through escrow gets the bill through the lender, and the Tax Collector notes that lenders must pay inside the 4 percent window.

The county counted 290,028 residents in July 2025, with 54.1 percent of homes owner occupied and a $288,800 median value in the 2020 to 2024 figures, which leaves a large renter base. With college-town turnover, ask the title company early for a tax and lien search.

faqs.q: When does Alachua County mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: Normally on or before November 1. If none arrives, the Tax Collector says to call (352) 374-5236.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Alachua County taxes without delinquency?
faqs.a: The full amount is due by the end of March. Delinquency starts April 1, with a 3 percent minimum charge.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Alachua County millage final?
faqs.a: The county's explainer calls it proposed. It shows 7.2107 mills as the proposed 2026 rollback rate against 7.6000 in 2025. Confirm the adopted rate with the Tax Collector or your bill.

faqs.q: Does selling my Alachua County home end my homestead?
faqs.a: A sale is a change of ownership, so the property goes back to just value the following January 1. The new owner files for their own exemption by March 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays delinquent tax and any certificate out of what the buyer sends. Ask the Tax Collector for the payoff amount before the closing date.
